Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a protocol into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme protocol and deliver a live timeline: Streaking Three Cultures onto Selective Media for three isolates, one purity plate
Resource limits: one loop station at the burner, one 37 °C incubator shelf holding two plates, one staining rack, one microscope, one technician, a supervisor signs off the readings.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Streaking Three Cultures onto Selective Media

Three overnight broths are streaked for single colonies on selective agar, incubated at 37 °C and read the next morning. The bench has one Bunsen burner with a single loop station, one 37 °C incubator with room for two plates on the free shelf, one staining rack and one microscope. One technician works the bench; a supervisor reads the plates before anything is subcultured.

Setup
1. Wipe the bench with 70 % ethanol and light the burner; 10 minutes.
2. Label three selective plates with the isolate number, the medium and the date; 10 minutes.

Streaking
3. Streak isolate 1 for single colonies in four quadrants, flaming the loop between each; 10 minutes.
4. Streak isolate 2 the same way; 10 minutes.
5. Streak isolate 3 the same way; 10 minutes.
6. Invert plates 1 and 2 and put them on the incubator shelf overnight, 16 to 20 hours.
7. Only two plates fit on the shelf, so hold plate 3 at room temperature on the bench until plate 1 comes out.
8. Incubate plate 3 at 37 °C for 6 hours once the shelf is free.

Reading
9. Read plate 1 in the morning: count the colonies, note the colour and record the selective growth; 15 minutes.
10. Read plate 2 the same way; 15 minutes.
11. Read plate 3 at the end of its run; 15 minutes.

Subculture and stain
12. Pick a single well-separated colony from each of plates 1 and 2 into fresh broth; 10 minutes at the loop station.
13. Do not streak the purity plate until the supervisor has signed off the readings. Streaking it takes 15 minutes.
14. Incubate the purity plate at 37 °C for 8 hours.
15. Make a smear from the picked colony and heat-fix it; 10 minutes.
16. Gram stain the smear on the rack: crystal violet, iodine, decolourise, safranin; 15 minutes.
17. Read the stain under oil immersion and record the morphology; 15 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. **Read-back.** This protocol cultures three bacterial isolates — presumably three separate overnight broths — onto selective agar so that each grows up as single colonies: the technician preps the bench (10 min wipe + flame, 10 min labelling three plates), streaks the three isolates one after another for ten minutes each with the loop flamed between quadrants, then incubates. Two plates go straight onto the one free 37 °C shelf for an overnight run of 16–20 hours; because the shelf only holds two, the third plate must be **held at room temperature on the bench** until plate 1 comes out, then incubated at 37 °C for 6 hours. In the morning the plates are read one at a time (15 min each: colony count, colour, selective growth), a single well-separated colony is picked from each of plates 1 and 2 into fresh broth (10 min at the loop station), and a **supervisor must sign off those readings before** a 15-minute streak of the **one purity plate**, which then incubates at 37 °C for 8 hours. In parallel with the reading/subculture line, the same picked colony is smeared and heat-fixed (10 min), Gram stained on the rack — crystal violet, iodine, decolourise, safranin (15 min) — and read under oil immersion for morphology (15 min). No wall-clock finish time was given, so the target is simply as early as the work allows: with a 16-hour minimum overnight incubation the run is inherently overnight-plus (roughly 16–17 h of incubation before anything can be read), and the tail is the purity plate's 8-hour incubation, plus plate 3's 6-hour run which starts only when plate 1 is pulled. The binding limits are the single technician's hands, the one loop station at the burner (serialising setup work, the three streaks, colony picking and the purity streak), the 37 °C shelf that holds exactly **two** plates (which is what forces plate 3 to be held on the bench), one staining rack, one microscope, and the supervisor as an external, unscheduled gate between the readings and the purity streak. Nothing in the text looks truncated — the numbered steps run 1 through 17 with no gaps and no referenced section missing, although the source does not say how the supervisor's sign-off is scheduled, how long plate 1 stays out before plate 3 goes in, or what happens to the purity plate after its 8-hour incubation (no read step is listed for it).
